claims.text: The starting material is gas-atomized FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy-alloy powder with a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
Increasing in-flight particle velocity during HVAF-i7 deposition will improve deposition efficiency.
A nozzle-to-substrate distance of 300–350 mm is an optimized range for HVAF-i7 deposition of FeCoNiCrAl.
The combined increase in particle velocity and use of a 300–350 mm spray distance will produce a thicker FeCoNiCrAl coating.
The resulting thicker coating will remain adherent.
The resulting coating will have minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The intervention can be applied when coating substrates with internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
FeCoNiCrAl coatings made under the proposed conditions can withstand thermal-barrier service at temperatures up to approximately 1100 °C.
Higher particle velocity increases particle kinetic energy and impact momentum.
Higher impact momentum causes particles to flatten and bond more effectively to the substrate.
Improved particle deformation and inter-splat bonding increase material retention and coating thickness.
A spray distance of 300–350 mm minimizes excessive in-flight oxidation.
A spray distance of 300–350 mm supplies sufficient heat for metallurgical bonding.
Relative to the previous HVAF-i7 process using the same 15–45 μm powder, the intervention will yield a statistically detectable increase in coating thickness.
The thicker coating will retain adhesion and microstructural integrity relative to the baseline.
The oxidation behavior of the proposed FeCoNiCrAl coating will be controlled similarly to that of MCrAlY coatings.
AlCoCrFeNi-based coatings have demonstrated high-temperature protective or oxidation-related behavior.
The prior HVAF-i7 baseline yields acceptable coating quality but inadequate thickness.
The intervention should remain effective on both flat surfaces and restricted internal geometries.
The proposed parameter transfer from conventional MCrAlY deposition to FeCoNiCrAl may require alloy-specific fine-tuning.

contradictions.description: The required 300–350 mm nozzle-to-substrate distance is not reconciled with direct coating of an internal wall having only a 120 mm diameter. As written, the claimed applicability to that restricted geometry is geometrically incompatible or at least severely under-specified.
